decisions.choice: oracle: a solemn pronouncement from God, here a word of judgment on a city
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "lift up": a word lifted up, that is, pronounced. It heads many of the prophets' words against the nations (Isaiah 13:1; 15:1; 17:1), and Habakkuk 1:1 opens the same way. It can also mean a load that is carried, a "burden", but here it names the kind of message that follows (see Isaiah 13:1).

decisions.choice: Nineveh: the capital of the Assyrian empire, destroyed in 612 BC
decisions.reason: Nineveh stood on the east bank of the Tigris, opposite modern Mosul in Iraq. Under Sennacherib (about 705-681 BC) it became the capital of Assyria, the empire that destroyed the northern kingdom of Israel in 722 BC and made Judah pay tribute (2 Kings 17-19). In 612 BC an alliance of Babylonians and Medes besieged the city and destroyed it, and the empire collapsed a few years later. Nahum's three chapters announce that fall. They were spoken after the fall of Thebes in Egypt (3:8-10, about 663 BC) and before 612 BC. A century or so earlier, in the book of Jonah, the same city had repented and been spared (Jonah 3:10).

decisions.choice: Nahum the Elkoshite: Nahum from the town of Elkosh, whose site is unknown
decisions.reason: The name Nahum means "comfort" or "comforter", a fitting name for a prophet whose message is comfort for Judah (1:12-13; 2:1). "Elkoshite" names his home town. Several places have been suggested, in Galilee, in Judah and near Nineveh, but none can be shown to be right. Nothing else is known about him.

decisions.choice: the book of the vision: a written record of what the prophet saw
decisions.reason: "Vision" is the usual word for a prophet's message from God, as in Isaiah 1:1 and Obadiah 1, whether it came by sight or by word. This is the only heading among the prophets that calls the message a "book", a written scroll, which may mean that it was written down from the start.

decisions.choice: An oracle (B); a message (R); of Elkosh (B); from Elkosh (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 13:1, Literal and Balanced say "oracle" and Readable says "message". Balanced and Readable say "of" or "from Elkosh" for "the Elkoshite", and Readable says that Nahum received the vision.

decisions.choice: "Oráculo sobre Nínive" (L, B); "Este es un mensaje sobre Nínive" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled Spanish heading for massa in the prophets.

decisions.reason: As the term sheet for massa and for the prophet's name.

decisions.choice: Nahum's poem is speech at every level: present, future and passé composé, never passé simple; Nineveh, addressed as a woman, takes "tu" and feminine agreement; the Lord's pronouns take deity_pronoun spans except at the start of a sentence
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for the prophets and for personified cities (Nahum 2-3).

decisions.choice: "Unabii [juu ya]" (L); "Unabii kuhusu" (B); "ujumbe kuhusu" (R)
decisions.reason: Massa' (oracle) as in Isaiah and the term sheet.

decisions.choice: "Sấm ngôn" (L, B); "sứ điệp" (R) for "massa'"
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for "massa'" in Nahum 1:1; "Na-hum người Ên-cốc" is the terms note's form of the name. Book-wide choices for Nahum (CHÚA spans, "Chúa là CHÚA", no quotation marks for God's oracles, Nineveh as "nó" and "ngươi") follow Micah 1:1 in this job.

decisions.choice: *massa'*: "신탁" (L, B), "…에 관한 말씀" (R); "엘고스 사람 나훔"
decisions.reason: As the term sheets for the oracle [2 Kings 9:25] and the names of the Twelve. Every YHWH in Nahum is the divine_name span with the particle outside; "여호와" is not used, and Korean has no deity_pronoun spans, the honorific carrying the respect.

decisions.choice: "Nahúm el elcosita" (L); "Nahúm de Elcos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The forms set by the term sheet, on the pattern of "Miqueas el morastita" / "de Moréset".

decisions.choice: "Nahumu Mwelkoshi" (L); "Nahumu wa Elkoshi" (B); "Nahumu kutoka Elkoshi" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms; the town takes the usual Swahili ending, as Micah's "Mmoreshethi" / "wa Moreshethi".

decisions.choice: Oráculo [sobre] Nínive (L); Mensagem sobre Nínive (B); Esta é uma mensagem sobre Nínive (R); o livro da visão de Naum, o elcosita (L); Naum, de Elcos (B); da cidade de Elcos (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the heading takes the formula of Isaiah 13:1 in Portuguese for massa' (m1), "oráculo" at Literal and "mensagem" at Balanced and Readable, with "sobre" where the English says "concerning" and "about". "Visão" is the noun of Isaiah 1:1 and Obadiah 1 (m4). The prophet's town takes the pattern of Micah 1:1 ("Miqueias, o morastita" / "de Moresete"): "o elcosita" at Literal, "de Elcos" at Balanced and Readable.

ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 질투하시며 원수를 갚으시는 하나님이시다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 원수를 갚으시며 진노가 가득하시다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 그분의 대적들에게 원수를 갚으시고, \q 그분의 원수들에게 노여움을 품으신다.

pt.L: Deus zeloso e vingador [é] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}; \q vingador [é] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, e senhor de furor; \q {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} se vinga dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} adversários, \q e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} guarda [o furor] para os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} inimigos.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é um Deus zeloso e vingador; \q {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} se vinga e está cheio de furor. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} se vinga dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} adversários \q e mantém a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira contra os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} inimigos.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é um Deus zeloso, que castiga o mal. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} castiga, e a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira é terrível. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} castiga os que se opõem a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. \q Ele continua irado com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} inimigos.

decisions.choice: verses 2-8 are a partial alphabet poem, from aleph to kaph
alternatives: no acrostic was intended, and the letters fall in order by chance
decisions.reason: Lines in these verses begin, more or less in order, with the letters of the Hebrew alphabet: aleph in verse 2, beth in the second half of verse 3, gimel in verse 4, then he and waw in verse 5, zayin and heth in verse 6, teth and yod in verse 7, and kaph in verse 8. The pattern is not complete: the letter for daleth in verse 4 is missing (see the note there), some letters stand at the second word of a line rather than the first, and after kaph the order breaks off. Some readers trace it further into verses 9-14, but only by changing the text. How far the poem was meant as an acrostic, and whether it once ran through the whole alphabet, cannot be known. Like the acrostics of Lamentations, it gives the poem a sense of order and completeness: the LORD's judgment is full and orderly, from first to last.

decisions.choice: jealous: zealous for the loyalty that belongs to him alone
decisions.reason: This form of the word is used only here and in Joshua 24:19. A related form is in the commandments: "I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God" (Exodus 20:5; 34:14). It is the passion of one who will not share what belongs to him: the loyalty of his people, and his own honor. It also turns to protect his people against those who attack them (Zechariah 1:14-15; Joel 2:18). It is not petty envy.

decisions.choice: avenging: punishing wrongs as a ruler and judge does
decisions.reason: The verb, used three times in a row, is the act of a king or judge who sees that a wrong is punished and the wronged are set right. Scripture forbids people to take revenge for themselves and leaves vengeance to God (Leviticus 19:18; Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19). Here the wrong is Assyria's cruelty to the nations and to Judah (3:1, 19).

decisions.choice: a master of wrath ... keeps wrath: his anger is real and does not simply lapse
decisions.reason: "Master of wrath" is a Hebrew way of saying that someone is full of wrath, as "master of dreams" (Genesis 37:19) means a dreamer. "Keep" with no object is used of keeping anger (Leviticus 19:18; Psalm 103:9; Jeremiah 3:5): he holds it against his enemies. The next verse balances this: he is slow to anger.

decisions.choice: a master of wrath (L); full of wrath (B); his anger is fierce (R); keeps [wrath] (L); holds his anger (B); stays angry (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture and brackets the word "wrath", which the verb implies. Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m4). Readable says "punishes" for "avenges", because "revenge" in English suggests personal spite (m3), and adds "wrongdoing" to make the object plain.

decisions.choice: "señor de furor" (L); "lleno de furor" (B); "su enojo es terrible" (R)
decisions.reason: Ḥemah is "furor" at Literal and Balanced and "enojo" at Readable, as the term sheet sets.

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" by default, "Yahvé" with the setting; God's pronouns and possessives ("il", "lui", "sa", "ses") under deity_pronoun
decisions.reason: As in all the prophets: the span takes in the article ("du SEIGNEUR", "au SEIGNEUR"), and a possessive agrees with its noun ("sa fureur"). "Je" for God takes no span. This holds for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "Mungu mwenye wivu"
decisions.reason: The LORD's jealousy is his zeal for the loyalty owed to him alone (meaning decision), the same words as the Swahili of Exodus 20:5. The alphabet pattern of 1:2-8 is not imitated at any level; the English meaning decision names it.

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời kỵ tà", as the published Exodus 34:14
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: zealous for the loyalty that belongs to him alone; "kỵ tà" is the word Vietnamese Exodus uses, and "ghen tuông" would suggest a jealous lover.

decisions.choice: "질투하시는 하나님", "원수를 갚으시다" (L, B); "벌하시다" (R)
decisions.reason: "질투하는 하나님" is the published wording of the commandments [Exod 20:5]; here the prophet speaks about God, so it takes -시-. Avenging is a ruler's punishing of wrongs (meaning decision); Readable says "벌하다".

decisions.choice: the partial alphabet poem of 1:2-8 is not imitated
decisions.reason: The meaning footnote: verses 2-8 run from aleph to kaph. Vietnamese cannot keep a Hebrew letter order, so the lines follow the sense and the footnote tells the reader.

decisions.choice: no level imitates the partial alphabet poem of 1:2-8
decisions.reason: As in Lamentations, the acrostic is described in the meaning decision and not reproduced in Spanish.

decisions.choice: No Korean acrostic in 1:2-8
decisions.reason: Verses 2-8 are a partial alphabet poem (meaning decision, footnoted). Korean cannot follow the Hebrew letters, so the footnote carries it and each verse keeps its own content; the letter names stay in the English decision text. Marked uncertain in the English, as the extent of the acrostic is debated.

decisions.choice: "kulipiza kisasi" (L, B); "kuadhibu" (R)
decisions.reason: Vengeance as the just punishment a ruler and judge gives, as Isaiah 1:24 and Micah 5:14; Readable says "punish", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Deus zeloso e vingador (L, B); um Deus zeloso, que castiga o mal (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "zeloso", from "zelo", is the word Exodus 20:5 and 34:14 and Ezekiel use in Portuguese for God's jealousy, the passion of one who will not share what is his (m2); "ciumento" sounds petty. "Vingador" names one who avenges a wrong as judge (m3), where "vingativo" would name a spiteful temper. Readable says "castiga", as the English Readable says "punishes".

decisions.choice: senhor de furor; guarda [o furor]
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture "senhor de furor" (m4), lowercase since it is not a title, and brackets the object of "guarda", as the English Literal brackets "wrath".

source.text: יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֨יִם֙ וּגְדָל־כֹּ֔חַ וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֣א יְנַקֶּ֑ה יְהוָ֗ה בְּסוּפָ֤ה וּבִשְׂעָרָה֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְעָנָ֖ן אֲבַ֥ק רַגְלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh [is] long of anger and great of power, and to leave unpunished not he will leave unpunished. Yahweh, in storm-wind and in storm [is] his way, and clouds [are the] dust of his feet.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] long of anger and great in power, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will by no means acquit [the guilty]. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, in whirlwind and in storm [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way, \q and clouds [are] the dust of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is slow to grow angry but great in power, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will never acquit the guilty. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way in the whirlwind and the storm, \q and the clouds are the dust of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is slow to become angry, but {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power is great. \q He will not let the guilty go free. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} travels in the whirlwind and the storm. \q The clouds are like dust kicked up by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [es] lento para la ira y grande en poder, \q y de ningún modo absolverá [al culpable]. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: en el torbellino y en la tempestad [está] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} camino, \q y las nubes [son] el polvo de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es lento para enojarse, pero grande en poder, \q y nunca declarará inocente al culpable. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se abre camino en el torbellino y en la tempestad, \q y las nubes son el polvo de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no se enoja fácilmente, pero {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder es grande. \q No dejará que el culpable quede libre. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} viaja en el torbellino y en la tormenta. \q Las nubes son como el polvo que levantan {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] lent à la colère et grand en puissance, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne tient nullement [le coupable] pour innocent. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, dans le tourbillon et dans la tempête [est] {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} chemin, \q et les nuées [sont] la poussière de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est lent à {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} mettre en colère, mais grand en puissance, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne déclare jamais innocent le coupable. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}avance dans le tourbillon et la tempête, \q et les nuées sont la poussière de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} met pas vite en colère, mais {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance est grande. \q Il ne laisse pas le coupable impuni. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} voyage dans le tourbillon et la tempête. \q Les nuages sont comme la poussière que soulèvent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] mkawivu wa hasira na mkuu wa nguvu, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} hamhesabu kamwe [mwenye hatia] kuwa hana hatia. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, katika kisulisuli na katika dhoruba [iko] njia {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q na mawingu [ni] mavumbi ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anachelewa kukasirika lakini ni mkuu wa nguvu, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} hamtangazi kamwe mwenye hatia kuwa hana hatia. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hufanya njia {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} katika kisulisuli na dhoruba, \q nayo mawingu ni mavumbi ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakasiriki upesi, lakini nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} ni kuu. \q Hamwachi mwenye hatia aende huru. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} husafiri katika kisulisuli na dhoruba. \q Mawingu ni kama mavumbi yanayotimuliwa na miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [là] Đấng chậm giận và quyền năng lớn lao, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chẳng hề coi [kẻ có tội] là vô tội. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đường lối {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [ở] trong gió lốc và trong bão tố, \q và mây [là] bụi dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chậm nóng giận nhưng quyền năng lớn lao, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không bao giờ coi kẻ có tội là vô tội. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mở đường đi giữa gió lốc và bão tố, \q và mây là bụi dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chậm giận, nhưng quyền năng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thật lớn lao. \q Ngài không để kẻ có tội được thoát. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đi trong gió lốc và bão tố. \q Mây như bụi tung lên dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 분노를 오래 참으시나 능력이 크시며, \q [죄 있는 자를] 결코 죄 없다 하지 않으신다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 회오리바람과 폭풍 속에 그분의 길이 있고, \q 구름은 그분의 발의 티끌이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 쉽게 노하지 않으시나 능력이 크시며, \q 죄 있는 사람을 결코 죄 없다 하지 않으신다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 회오리바람과 폭풍 속에서 길을 가시고, \q 구름은 그분의 발에서 이는 티끌이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 좀처럼 화를 내지 않으시지만, 그분의 능력은 크다. \q 그분께서는 죄지은 사람을 그냥 내버려 두지 않으신다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 회오리바람과 폭풍 속을 다니신다. \q 구름은 그분의 발에서 일어나는 먼지와 같다.

pt.L: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} [é] longo de ira e grande em poder, \q e de modo nenhum {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} inocentará [o culpado]. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}: no redemoinho e na tempestade [está] o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} caminho, \q e as nuvens [são] o pó dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é lento para se irar, mas grande em poder, \q e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} jamais deixará impune o culpado. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} faz o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} caminho no redemoinho e na tempestade, \q e as nuvens são o pó dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} demora a ficar irado, mas o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} poder é grande. \q Ele não vai deixar o culpado ficar sem castigo. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} anda no redemoinho e na tempestade. \q As nuvens são como a poeira que os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés levantam.

decisions.choice: slow to anger ... will by no means acquit: the words of Exodus 34:6-7, with "great in power" in place of "great in loyal love"
decisions.reason: When the LORD proclaimed his name to Moses he said that he is "slow to anger and great in loyal love and faithfulness", forgiving sin, "but he will by no means acquit the guilty" (Exodus 34:6-7). Joel 2:13 and Jonah 4:2 quote the merciful side of these words. Nahum quotes the start and the end, and where Exodus says "great in loyal love" he says "great in power". The point is not that God has stopped being merciful (verse 7 says he is good to those who trust him), but that his patience is not weakness. Jonah complained that God's mercy spared Nineveh (Jonah 4:2); Nahum announces that the same God will not leave the city's guilt unpunished for ever.

decisions.choice: will by no means acquit: the verb repeated for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "and leaving unpunished, he will not leave unpunished", a verb doubled to make it certain, the same phrase as Exodus 34:7. The object, "the guilty", is not stated but is plain from Exodus.

decisions.choice: whirlwind, storm and clouds: the LORD comes as in a great storm
decisions.reason: Scripture often pictures the LORD's coming to judge or rescue as a storm, with wind, cloud, thunder and an earthquake (Exodus 19:16-18; Psalm 18:8-16; Habakkuk 3). Clouds are his chariot (Psalm 104:3); here they are the dust his feet kick up, so great is he.

decisions.choice: long of anger (L), slow to grow angry (B), slow to become angry (R); will by no means acquit (L), will never acquit (B), will not let the guilty go free (R)
decisions.reason: These are the words of Exodus 34:6-7 as already published, kept at each level so that the reader hears the echo (m1). Where Exodus has *hesed* Nahum has "power", so the open question of how to word *hesed* in these quotations does not touch this verse. The prophets use "loyal love" (Literal, Balanced) and "faithful love" (Readable), pending the founder's ruling; the published Exodus 34:6 has "steadfast love" at Literal. Literal brackets "the guilty", which the Hebrew leaves unstated.

decisions.choice: like dust kicked up by his feet
decisions.reason: Readable adds "like" and "kicked up" so that the picture is not read as a statement that clouds are dust.

decisions.choice: "lento para la ira ... de ningún modo absolverá [al culpable]" (L); "lento para enojarse ... nunca declarará inocente al culpable" (B); "no se enoja fácilmente ... No dejará que el culpable quede libre" (R)
decisions.reason: The verse echoes Exodus 34:6-7, so each level reuses the published Spanish of those verses, with "grande en poder" where Exodus 34:6 has "grande en amor fiel".

decisions.choice: The published Exodus 34:6-7 at each level: "lent à la colère ... ne tient nullement [le coupable] pour innocent" (L), "lent à se mettre en colère ... ne déclare jamais innocent le coupable" (B), "ne se met pas vite en colère ... ne laisse pas le coupable impuni" (R), with "grand en puissance" where Exodus has "grand en amour fidèle"
decisions.reason: Nahum quotes Exodus 34:6-7, as the English meaning decision says; French reuses the published words and changes only what Nahum changes.

decisions.choice: The published words of Exodus 34:6-7 at each level ("mkawivu wa hasira", "hamhesabu kamwe [mwenye hatia] kuwa hana hatia" L; "anachelewa kukasirika", "hamtangazi kamwe mwenye hatia kuwa hana hatia" B; "hakasiriki upesi", "hamwachi mwenye hatia aende huru" R)
decisions.reason: Nahum quotes the LORD's self-description (term sheet: Nahum 1:3 reuses Exodus 34:6), with "great in power" where Exodus has "great in loyal love"; the Swahili changes only that.

decisions.choice: "chậm giận" (L, R) / "chậm nóng giận" (B), and "chẳng hề coi [kẻ có tội] là vô tội" (L) / "không bao giờ coi kẻ có tội là vô tội" (B) / "không để kẻ có tội được thoát" (R), as the published Exodus 34:6-7
decisions.reason: The terms note: Nahum 1:3 reuses the published Exodus wording; the meaning decision says Nahum puts "great in power" where Exodus has "great in loyal love", and the Vietnamese changes only that.

decisions.choice: The phrases of the Korean Exodus 34:6-7 at each level ("분노를 오래 참고", "결코 죄 없다 하지 않고" L; "쉽게 노하지 않으며", "결코 죄 없다 하지 않고" B; "좀처럼 화를 내지 않는", "그냥 내버려 두지는 않는다" R), with "능력이 크다" for Nahum's "great in power"
decisions.reason: The verse echoes Exodus 34:6-7 and changes "great in loyal love" to "great in power" (meaning decision); Korean reuses the published Exodus wording so the echo and the change are both visible, with -시- because the prophet speaks about God.

decisions.choice: longo de ira (L), lento para se irar (B), demora a ficar irado (R); de modo nenhum inocentará [o culpado] (L), jamais deixará impune o culpado (B), não vai deixar o culpado ficar sem castigo (R)
decisions.reason: Nahum takes up the words of Exodus 34:6-7 (m1), so each level keeps the Portuguese of Exodus, as Joel 2:13 does, in the future where Nahum's verb looks ahead; only "grande em poder" stands where Exodus has "amor leal".

decisions.choice: como a poeira que os seus pés levantam
decisions.reason: As in the English Readable, "como" and "levantam" keep the picture from reading as a statement that clouds are dust.

source.text: גּוֹעֵ֤ר בַּיָּם֙ וַֽיַּבְּשֵׁ֔הוּ וְכָל־הַנְּהָר֖וֹת הֶֽחֱרִ֑יב אֻמְלַ֤ל בָּשָׁן֙ וְכַרְמֶ֔ל וּפֶ֥רַח לְבָנ֖וֹן אֻמְלָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Rebuking the sea and he dried it up, and all the rivers he has dried up; withered [are] Bashan and Carmel, and [the] blossom of Lebanon has withered.

en.L: He rebukes the sea and makes it dry, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dries up all the rivers; \q Bashan and Carmel wither, \q and the bloom of Lebanon withers.
en.B: He rebukes the sea and makes it dry; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dries up every river. \q Bashan and Carmel wilt, \q and the flowers of Lebanon fade.
en.R: He gives an order to the sea, and it dries up. \q He makes all the rivers run dry. \q The rich pastures of Bashan and Carmel dry up, \q and the flowers of Lebanon wither.

es.L: Reprende al mar y lo seca, \q y agota todos los ríos; \q Basán y el Carmelo se marchitan, \q y la flor del Líbano se marchita.
es.B: Reprende al mar y lo deja seco; \q hace que se sequen todos los ríos. \q Basán y el Carmelo se marchitan, \q y las flores del Líbano se desvanecen.
es.R: Le da una orden al mar, y se seca. \q Hace que todos los ríos se queden sin agua. \q Los ricos pastos de Basán y del Carmelo se secan, \q y las flores del Líbano se marchitan.

fr.L: Il menace la mer et la dessèche, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} tarit tous les fleuves ; \q le Bashân et le Carmel se flétrissent, \q et la fleur du Liban se flétrit.
fr.B: Il menace la mer et la met à sec ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} tarit tous les fleuves. \q Le Bashân et le Carmel dépérissent, \q et les fleurs du Liban se fanent.
fr.R: Il donne un ordre à la mer, et elle s’assèche. \q Il met tous les fleuves à sec. \q Les riches pâturages du Bashân et du Carmel se dessèchent, \q et les fleurs du Liban se fanent.

sw.L: Huikemea bahari na kuikausha, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} huikausha mito yote; \q Bashani na Karmeli hunyauka, \q na maua ya Lebanoni hunyauka.
sw.B: Huikemea bahari na kuikausha; \q huikausha kila mto. \q Bashani na Karmeli hunyauka, \q na maua ya Lebanoni hufifia.
sw.R: Huipa bahari amri, nayo hukauka. \q Huifanya mito yote ikauke. \q Malisho mazuri ya Bashani na Karmeli hukauka, \q na maua ya Lebanoni hunyauka.

vi.L: Ngài quở trách biển và làm cho nó khô cạn, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm khô hết các sông; \q Ba-san và Cạt-mên héo úa, \q và hoa của Li-ban tàn héo.
vi.B: Ngài quở biển và làm cho nó khô cạn; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm mọi dòng sông cạn khô. \q Ba-san và Cạt-mên héo hon, \q và hoa Li-ban tàn úa.
vi.R: Ngài ra lệnh cho biển, và biển liền khô cạn. \q Ngài làm cho mọi dòng sông cạn khô. \q Các đồng cỏ xanh tốt của Ba-san và Cạt-mên khô héo, \q và hoa của Li-ban tàn úa.

ko.L: 그분께서는 바다를 꾸짖어 마르게 하시고, \q 모든 강을 말리신다. \q 바산과 갈멜이 시들고, \q 레바논의 꽃이 시든다.
ko.B: 그분께서 바다를 꾸짖어 마르게 하시고, \q 모든 강을 말려 버리신다. \q 바산과 갈멜이 시들고, \q 레바논의 꽃이 시들어 버린다.
ko.R: 그분께서 바다에 명령하시면 바다가 말라 버린다. \q 그분께서 모든 강을 마르게 하신다. \q 바산과 갈멜의 기름진 목초지가 말라 버리고, \q 레바논의 꽃들이 시든다.

pt.L: Ele repreende o mar e o seca, \q e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} faz secar todos os rios; \q murcham Basã e o Carmelo, \q e a flor do Líbano murcha.
pt.B: Ele repreende o mar e o faz secar; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} seca todos os rios. \q Basã e o Carmelo definham, \q e as flores do Líbano murcham.
pt.R: Ele dá uma ordem ao mar, e o mar seca. \q Ele faz secar todos os rios. \q Os ricos pastos de Basã e do Carmelo secam, \q e as flores do Líbano murcham.

decisions.choice: rebuking the sea and drying the rivers: the LORD's power over the waters
decisions.reason: The LORD "rebuked the Red Sea and it dried up" when Israel left Egypt (Psalm 106:9), and the Jordan stopped flowing before them (Joshua 3:16). The same words are used of his power over the sea and the floods in Isaiah 50:2 and Psalm 104:7. In the poetry of the ancient world the sea stood for the forces of chaos; the LORD commands it with a word.

decisions.choice: Bashan, Carmel and Lebanon: the most fertile places in the land
decisions.reason: Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee, was famous for its cattle and oaks (Amos 4:1; Isaiah 2:13); Carmel, the ridge by the sea, for its gardens and woods; Lebanon for its cedars and flowers. If even these wither when the LORD comes, nothing can stand before him. Isaiah 33:9 names the same places.

decisions.choice: withers ... withers: the same verb twice
alternatives: a different verb meaning "languish", beginning with daleth
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the same verb at the start and the end of the second line. In the alphabet pattern of verses 2-8 (see verse 2), the first of them stands where a word beginning with daleth is expected. A verb of the same sense that begins with that letter has therefore been suggested in its place. No change in the sense follows, and the translation keeps the text as it stands.

decisions.choice: gives an order to (R); the rich pastures of (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "gives an order" for "rebukes", since the sea obeys a command, and adds "the rich pastures of" so that the reader knows why Bashan and Carmel are named (m2).

decisions.choice: "se marchitan ... se marchita" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal repeats one verb, as the Hebrew does.

source.text: הָרִים֙ רָעֲשׁ֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְהַגְּבָע֖וֹת הִתְמֹגָ֑גוּ וַתִּשָּׂ֤א הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ מִפָּנָ֔יו וְתֵבֵ֖ל וְכָל־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] mountains quake because of him, and the hills melt; and the earth heaves up from before him, and [the] world and all [who] dwell in it.

en.L: [The] mountains quake because of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and the hills melt; \q the earth heaves before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q the world and all who dwell in it.
en.B: Before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the mountains quake, \q and the hills melt away. \q The earth heaves at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence, \q the world and everyone who lives in it.
en.R: The mountains shake when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes, \q and the hills melt away. \q The earth trembles when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appears, \q the whole world and everyone who lives in it.

es.L: Los montes tiemblan ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q y las colinas se derriten; \q la tierra se levanta delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q el mundo y todos los que habitan en él.
es.B: Ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tiemblan los montes \q y las colinas se derriten. \q La tierra se estremece en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia, \q el mundo y todos los que viven en él.
es.R: Los montes tiemblan cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} viene, \q y las colinas se derriten. \q La tierra se sacude cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} aparece, \q el mundo entero y todos los que viven en él.

fr.L: Les montagnes tremblent à cause de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \q et les collines fondent ; \q la terre se soulève devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \q le monde et tous ceux qui l’habitent.
fr.B: Devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, les montagnes tremblent \q et les collines se fondent. \q La terre se soulève en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} présence, \q le monde et tous ceux qui l’habitent.
fr.R: Les montagnes tremblent quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} arrive, \q et les collines fondent. \q La terre tremble quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} paraît, \q le monde entier et tous ceux qui y vivent.

sw.L: Milima hutetemeka kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q na vilima huyeyuka; \q dunia huinuka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q ulimwengu na wote wakaao ndani yake.
sw.B: Mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} milima hutetemeka, \q na vilima huyeyuka. \q Dunia hutikisika mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q ulimwengu na kila mtu anayeishi ndani yake.
sw.R: Milima hutikisika anapokuja, \q na vilima huyeyuka. \q Dunia hutetemeka anapotokea, \q ulimwengu wote na kila mtu anayeishi ndani yake.

vi.L: Núi non rúng động vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và các đồi tan chảy; \q đất phồng lên trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q thế gian và mọi người sống trong đó.
vi.B: Trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, núi non rung chuyển, \q và đồi nổng tan chảy. \q Đất dậy sóng trước sự hiện diện của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q cả thế gian cùng mọi người sống trong đó.
vi.R: Núi non rung chuyển khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, \q và đồi nổng tan chảy. \q Đất rúng động khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hiện ra, \q cả thế gian và mọi người sống trên đất.

ko.L: 그분 때문에 산들이 진동하고, \q 언덕들이 녹으며, \q 그분 앞에서 땅이 들썩인다, \q 세상과 그 안에 사는 모든 자가.
ko.B: 그분 앞에서 산들이 흔들리고, \q 언덕들이 녹아내린다. \q 그분 앞에서 땅이 들썩이고, \q 세상과 그 안에 사는 모든 사람이 떤다.
ko.R: 그분께서 오시면 산들이 흔들리고, \q 언덕들이 녹아내린다. \q 그분께서 나타나시면 땅이 떤다. \q 온 세상과 그 안에 사는 모든 사람이 떤다.

pt.L: Os montes tremem por causa {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, \q e as colinas se derretem; \q a terra se ergue diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, \q o mundo e todos os que nele habitam.
pt.B: Diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} os montes tremem, \q e as colinas se derretem. \q A terra se sacode na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} presença, \q o mundo e todos os que vivem nele.
pt.R: Os montes tremem quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vem, \q e as colinas se derretem. \q A terra estremece quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} aparece, \q o mundo inteiro e todos os que vivem nele.

decisions.choice: mountains quake and hills melt: the earth's response to God's coming
decisions.reason: The same picture is in Judges 5:5, Psalm 97:5 and Micah 1:4. It does not describe one particular earthquake but the trembling of the whole creation before its maker when he comes to judge.

decisions.choice: the earth heaves: it rises and shakes as in an earthquake
alternatives: the earth is laid waste before him
decisions.reason: The verb means "lift up". Used of the earth, it pictures the ground heaving. Some take it as "the earth is laid waste" by reading a verb of similar sound, but the plain sense of the word fits the quaking mountains.

decisions.choice: when he comes; when he appears
decisions.reason: Readable says "when he comes" and "when he appears" for "before him", since the verses describe the LORD's coming (verse 3).

source.text: לִפְנֵ֤י זַעְמוֹ֙ מִ֣י יַֽעֲמ֔וֹד וּמִ֥י יָק֖וּם בַּחֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ חֲמָתוֹ֙ נִתְּכָ֣ה כָאֵ֔שׁ וְהַצֻּרִ֖ים נִתְּצ֥וּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Before his indignation who can stand? And who can rise up in [the] burning of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are torn down by him.

en.L: Before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} indignation, who can stand? \q And who can endure the burning of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger? \q His fury is poured out as fire, \q and the rocks are torn apart by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Who can stand before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} indignation? \q Who can endure {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger? \q His wrath pours out like fire, \q and the rocks are shattered before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Who can stand up to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fury? \q Who can survive when {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger burns? \q His anger pours out like fire. \q He breaks the rocks to pieces.

es.L: Ante {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} indignación, ¿quién podrá estar en pie? \q ¿Y quién resistirá el ardor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira? \q Su furor se derrama como fuego, \q y las rocas son despedazadas por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: ¿Quién podrá mantenerse en pie ante {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} indignación? \q ¿Quién resistirá el ardor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira? \q Su furor se derrama como fuego, \q y las rocas se hacen pedazos ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: ¿Quién puede hacer frente a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} furia? \q ¿Quién puede sobrevivir cuando {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enojo arde? \q Su enojo se derrama como fuego. \q Él hace pedazos las rocas.

fr.L: Devant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} indignation, qui tiendra debout ? \q Et qui résistera à l’ardeur de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère ? \q Sa fureur se répand comme le feu, \q et les rochers sont brisés par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Qui tiendra debout devant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} indignation ? \q Qui supportera {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère ardente ? \q Sa fureur se répand comme un feu, \q et les rochers volent en éclats devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Qui peut résister à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} fureur ? \q Qui peut survivre quand {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère s’enflamme ? \q Sa colère se répand comme un feu. \q Il brise les rochers en morceaux.

sw.L: Mbele ya ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ni nani awezaye kusimama? \q Na ni nani awezaye kustahimili ukali wa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}? \q Ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inamwagwa kama moto, \q na miamba inavunjwa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.B: Ni nani awezaye kusimama mbele ya ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}? \q Ni nani awezaye kustahimili hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kali? \q Ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inamwagika kama moto, \q na miamba inapasuka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Ni nani awezaye kushindana na ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}? \q Ni nani atakayebaki hai hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inapowaka? \q Hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inamwagika kama moto. \q Anaivunja miamba vipande vipande.

vi.L: Trước cơn phẫn nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, ai đứng nổi? \q Ai chịu được cơn giận phừng phừng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}? \q Cơn thịnh nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đổ ra như lửa, \q và các vầng đá bị {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đập tan.
vi.B: Ai đứng nổi trước cơn phẫn nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}? \q Ai chịu nổi cơn giận nóng cháy của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}? \q Cơn thịnh nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tuôn đổ như lửa, \q và đá tảng vỡ tan trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ai có thể chống lại cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}? \q Ai có thể sống sót khi cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bừng cháy? \q Cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đổ ra như lửa. \q Ngài đập vỡ đá ra từng mảnh.

ko.L: 그분의 분노 앞에 누가 설 수 있으며, \q 누가 그분의 타오르는 진노를 견딜 수 있겠느냐? \q 그분의 진노가 불처럼 쏟아지니, \q 바위들이 그분 때문에 깨어진다.
ko.B: 누가 그분의 분노 앞에 설 수 있겠느냐? \q 누가 그분의 타오르는 진노를 견딜 수 있겠느냐? \q 그분의 진노가 불처럼 쏟아지니, \q 바위들이 그분 앞에서 산산이 부서진다.
ko.R: 누가 그분의 분노를 당해 낼 수 있겠느냐? \q 그분의 분노가 타오를 때 누가 살아남을 수 있겠느냐? \q 그분의 분노가 불처럼 쏟아진다. \q 그분께서 바위들을 산산조각 내신다.

pt.L: Diante da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} indignação, quem pode ficar de pé? \q E quem pode resistir ao ardor da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira? \q O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} furor se derrama como fogo, \q e as rochas são despedaçadas por {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.
pt.B: Quem pode ficar de pé diante da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} indignação? \q Quem pode suportar o ardor da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira? \q O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} furor se derrama como fogo, \q e as rochas se despedaçam diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.R: Quem consegue enfrentar a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} fúria? \q Quem pode sobreviver quando a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira se acende? \q A {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira se derrama como fogo. \q Ele quebra as rochas em pedaços.

decisions.choice: who can stand ... who can endure: questions that expect the answer "no one"
decisions.reason: The questions are not asking for information. They declare that no one can withstand the LORD's anger, as in Joel 2:11, Malachi 3:2 and Psalm 76:8.

decisions.choice: poured out like fire ... the rocks are broken down
decisions.reason: Wrath poured out like fire suggests molten metal or lava flowing (compare Jeremiah 7:20). The second verb means to pull down or break apart, used of walls and altars (Judges 6:30-32); even rock, the most solid thing in nature, gives way.

decisions.choice: stand up to; survive when his anger burns
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the questions but uses everyday words: "stand up to" for standing before an opponent, and "survive" for "endure" or "rise up".

decisions.choice: wrath (*chemah*) "진노" (L, B), "분노" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: "진노 / 진노 / 분노"; "분노" for the indignation of the first line at every level.

source.text: ט֣וֹב יְהוָ֔ה לְמָע֖וֹז בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה וְיֹדֵ֖עַ חֹ֥סֵי בֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Good [is] Yahweh, for a refuge in a day of trouble; and [he is] knowing those [who] take refuge in him.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] good, \q a stronghold in [the] day of distress, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows those who take refuge in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good, \q a stronghold in the day of trouble; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows those who take refuge in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good. \q He is a safe place when trouble comes. \q He cares for those who run to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for safety.

es.L: Bueno [es] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q fortaleza en [el] día de la angustia, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} conoce a los que se refugian en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es bueno, \q una fortaleza en el día de la angustia; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} conoce a los que se refugian en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es bueno. \q Es un lugar seguro cuando llegan los problemas. \q Él cuida de los que corren a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} buscando protección.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] bon, \q une forteresse au jour de la détresse, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} connaît ceux qui se réfugient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est bon, \q une forteresse au jour de la détresse ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} connaît ceux qui se réfugient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est bon. \q Il est un abri sûr quand vient le malheur. \q Il prend soin de ceux qui courent vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour être protégés.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] mwema, \q ngome katika siku ya taabu, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} huwajua wale wanaokimbilia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mwema, \q ngome katika siku ya taabu; \q huwajua wale wanaomkimbilia ili kujificha {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mwema. \q Yeye ni mahali pa usalama wakati wa taabu. \q Huwatunza wale wanaomkimbilia ili wawe salama.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [là] tốt lành, \q [là] đồn lũy trong ngày hoạn nạn, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết những người nương náu nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thật tốt lành, \q là đồn lũy trong ngày hoạn nạn; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết những ai nương náu nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thật tốt lành. \q Ngài là nơi an toàn khi gặp hoạn nạn. \q Ngài chăm sóc những ai chạy đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để được che chở.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 선하시니, \q 고난의 날에 산성이 되시며, \q 그분께 피하는 자들을 아신다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 선하시다. \q 그분은 환난의 날에 피난처가 되시고, \q 그분께 피하는 사람들을 아신다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 좋으신 분이시다. \q 어려운 일이 닥칠 때 그분께서 안전한 곳이 되어 주신다. \q 그분께서는 그분께 피하는 사람들을 돌보신다.

pt.L: Bom [é] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q uma fortaleza no dia da angústia, \q e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} conhece os que se refugiam {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é bom, \q uma fortaleza no dia da aflição; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} conhece os que buscam refúgio {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é bom. \q Ele é um lugar seguro quando chegam tempos difíceis. \q Ele cuida dos que correm para {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} em busca de proteção.

decisions.choice: the LORD is good: the other side of the same power
decisions.reason: Between the storm of verses 2-6 and the flood of verse 8 the poem says that the LORD is good. The power that crushes his enemies is the shelter of those who trust him. The whole book holds these together: judgment on Nineveh is comfort for Judah.

decisions.choice: a stronghold in the day of trouble
decisions.reason: The word is a fortress or place of safety, used of God in Psalm 27:1; 31:3 and 37:39. "The day of trouble" is any time of distress (Psalm 50:15), here Assyria's oppression.

decisions.choice: knows: cares for and acknowledges as his own
decisions.reason: To "know" people often means to care for them and take them as one's own: "the LORD knows the way of the righteous" (Psalm 1:6; Amos 3:2). Those who "take refuge" in him are those who trust him, as in Psalm 2:12.

decisions.choice: a safe place; cares for; run to him for safety
decisions.reason: Readable says "safe place" for "stronghold", "cares for" for "knows" (m3) and "run to him for safety" for "take refuge in him".

decisions.choice: "아신다" (L, B); "돌보신다" (R) for "knows"
decisions.reason: To know here is to care for and own as his (meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep "알다", which in Korean Bibles carries that sense, and Readable says it.

source.text: וּבְשֶׁ֣טֶף עֹבֵ֔ר כָּלָ֖ה יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה מְקוֹמָ֑הּ וְאֹיְבָ֖יו יְרַדֶּף־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And with a flood passing over, a complete end he will make of her place, and his enemies he will pursue [into] darkness.

en.L: But with a flood passing over \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make a full end of her place, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will pursue {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies [into] darkness.
en.B: But with a rushing flood \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make an end of her place, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will drive {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies into darkness.
en.R: But like a flood that sweeps everything away, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will completely destroy the place where Nineveh stands. \q He will chase {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies into darkness.

es.L: Pero con una inundación arrolladora \q hará completo fin del lugar de ella, \q y perseguirá a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos [hasta] las tinieblas.
es.B: Pero con una inundación impetuosa \q acabará con el lugar de ella, \q y empujará a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos a las tinieblas.
es.R: Pero como una inundación que lo arrastra todo, \q destruirá por completo el lugar donde está Nínive. \q Perseguirá a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos hasta la oscuridad.

fr.L: Mais par un flot qui déborde, \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fera une destruction complète de son lieu, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} poursuivra {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} ennemis [dans] les ténèbres.
fr.B: Mais par un flot impétueux, \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} anéantira le lieu où elle se trouve, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} chassera {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} ennemis dans les ténèbres.
fr.R: Mais comme une inondation qui emporte tout, \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} détruira complètement l’endroit où se dresse Ninive. \q Il poursuivra {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} ennemis jusque dans les ténèbres.

sw.L: Lakini kwa gharika ipitayo \q atapakomesha kabisa mahali pake, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atawafuatia adui {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} [mpaka] gizani.
sw.B: Lakini kwa gharika ifurikayo \q atapakomesha mahali pake, \q na kuwafukuza adui {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} mpaka gizani.
sw.R: Lakini kama gharika inayofagia kila kitu, \q ataangamiza kabisa mahali ambapo Ninawi umesimama. \q Atawafukuza adui {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} mpaka gizani.

vi.L: Nhưng bằng cơn lụt tràn qua \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ tận diệt chỗ của nó, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ đuổi các kẻ thù {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [vào] bóng tối.
vi.B: Nhưng bằng một cơn lũ cuồn cuộn, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ tận diệt chỗ của nó, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ đuổi các kẻ thù {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào bóng tối.
vi.R: Nhưng như cơn lũ cuốn trôi mọi vật, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ hủy diệt hoàn toàn nơi thành Ni-ni-ve tọa lạc. \q Ngài sẽ đuổi các kẻ thù {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào bóng tối.

ko.L: 그러나 넘쳐흐르는 홍수로 \q 그분께서 그 성의 자리를 완전히 끝장내시고, \q 그분의 원수들을 어둠 속으로 쫓아내실 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 그분께서는 휩쓸어 가는 홍수로 \q 그 성의 자리를 끝장내시고, \q 그분의 원수들을 어둠 속으로 몰아내실 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 그분께서는 모든 것을 휩쓸어 가는 홍수처럼 \q 니느웨가 서 있는 자리를 완전히 멸망시키실 것이다. \q 그분께서는 원수들을 어둠 속으로 쫓아내실 것이다.

pt.L: Mas com uma inundação que passa \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fará um fim completo do lugar dela, \q e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} perseguirá os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} inimigos [até as] trevas.

pt.R: Mas, como uma inundação que leva tudo embora, \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai destruir completamente o lugar onde Nínive está. \q Ele vai perseguir os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} inimigos até a escuridão.

decisions.choice: her place: the site of the city, Nineveh
alternatives: those who rise up against him (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "her place". Nineveh, named in 1:1, is the "her" of the book (2:2, 8-9; 3:7), so this means the city and its site: the flood will leave no place where it stood. The Greek translation, with different vowels, reads "those who rise up against him", which matches "his enemies" in the next line. The translation follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: an overflowing flood: an overwhelming judgment
decisions.reason: A flood that sweeps over the land is a common picture of an invading army (Isaiah 8:7-8; Daniel 9:26). Nahum may also have in mind the waters that played a part in the fall of Nineveh (2:7, 9).

decisions.choice: he will pursue his enemies into darkness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets "darkness" after the verb with no preposition. It may mean that the LORD drives his enemies into darkness, or that darkness pursues them. Darkness here is death and ruin, the opposite of light and life.

decisions.choice: the place where Nineveh stands
decisions.reason: Readable names Nineveh, because "her place" has no clear reference in this verse without it (m1).

decisions.choice: "mahali pake" (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Her place" is Nineveh's site; Swahili "pake" shows no gender and refers to the city, so it takes no deity_pronoun span. Readable names Nineveh, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "그 성의 자리" (L, B) for "her place"
decisions.reason: The pronoun is the site of Nineveh (meaning decision, footnoted); Korean says "그 성" rather than a feminine pronoun, and Readable names the city.

decisions.choice: "chỗ của nó" for "her place"
decisions.reason: The meaning footnote: the site of Nineveh. The terms note: a foreign city is "nó"; "nàng" is kept for Zion.

en.R: What are you planning against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? \q He will put a complete end to it. \q Trouble will not come a second time.

vi.L: Các ngươi mưu tính gì nghịch cùng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? \q Ngài sẽ làm cho tận diệt; \q tai họa sẽ không nổi lên lần thứ hai.

vi.R: Các ngươi đang toan tính gì chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? \q Ngài sẽ chấm dứt hoàn toàn mọi việc ấy. \q Tai họa sẽ không đến lần thứ hai.

ko.L: 너희가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 거슬러 무엇을 꾀하느냐? \q 그분께서 완전히 끝장내실 것이니, \q 재앙이 두 번 일어나지 않을 것이다.

ko.R: 너희가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 거슬러 무엇을 계획하느냐? \q 그분께서 그것을 완전히 끝내 버리실 것이다. \q 재앙이 다시 오지 않을 것이다.

pt.L: Que tramam vocês contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}? \q Ele está fazendo um fim completo; \q a angústia não se levantará duas vezes.
pt.B: O que vocês estão tramando contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}? \q Ele dará um fim completo; \q a aflição não se levantará uma segunda vez.
pt.R: O que vocês estão planejando contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}? \q Ele vai acabar de vez com isso. \q A desgraça não vai vir uma segunda vez.

decisions.choice: What do you plot: a challenge to those who plan against the LORD
alternatives: Whatever you plot against the LORD, he will make an end of it
decisions.reason: The question may also be read as "Whatever you plot against the LORD, he will make an end of it". "You" is plural. It is most likely addressed to the Assyrians, whose plans against Judah were plans against the LORD (verse 11). Some take it as addressed to doubters in Judah, who thought the LORD could not deal with Assyria.

decisions.choice: trouble will not rise up twice: one blow will be enough
alternatives: the distress Assyria brought will not come again
decisions.reason: The line may mean that the LORD's blow on Assyria will be so complete that it will not need to be struck again (compare 1 Samuel 26:8), or that the distress Assyria brought on Judah will not come again (verse 12). Both point to a final end.

decisions.choice: planning; put a complete end to it
decisions.reason: Readable says "planning" for "plotting" and adds "to it", meaning the plotting.

decisions.choice: "{{plural_you:traman|tramáis}}" with plural_you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is plural, so the question takes the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: "các ngươi" at every level for those who plot against the LORD
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for the prophets: God's opponents, the nations and the guilty are addressed with "ngươi" / "các ngươi" at every level in rebuke. Judah in the promises of 1:12-13 is "ngươi" (L) and "con" (B, R).

records.literal_gloss: For [though] like thorns entangled, and like their drink drunken, they will be consumed like stubble dry fully.

en.L: For though [they are] like entangled thorns, \q and drunk as with their drink, \q they will be consumed \q like stubble fully dry.
en.B: Though they are like a tangle of thorns \q and drunk with their wine, \q they will be burned up \q like dry stubble.
en.R: They are like a tangle of thorn bushes, \q like drunkards soaked in wine. \q But they will be burned up \q like dry straw.

es.B: Aunque sean como una maraña de espinos \q y estén ebrios de su vino, \q serán consumidos por el fuego \q como paja seca.
es.R: Son como una maraña de arbustos espinosos, \q como borrachos empapados de vino. \q Pero serán quemados \q como paja seca.

fr.B: Même s’ils sont comme un fouillis d’épines \q et ivres de leur vin, \q ils seront consumés \q comme de la paille sèche.

vi.B: Dù chúng như bụi gai rối rắm \q và say sưa vì rượu của mình, \q chúng sẽ bị thiêu rụi \q như rơm rạ khô.

ko.L: 그들이 엉클어진 가시덤불 같고, \q 자기들의 술에 취한 것 같아도, \q 그들은 바싹 마른 그루터기처럼 \q 완전히 불살라질 것이다.
ko.B: 그들이 뒤엉킨 가시덤불 같고 \q 포도주에 취해 있어도, \q 그들은 마른 그루터기처럼 \q 불타 버릴 것이다.
ko.R: 그들은 뒤엉킨 가시덤불 같다. \q 술에 흠뻑 취한 술꾼들 같다. \q 그러나 그들은 마른 지푸라기처럼 \q 타 버릴 것이다.

pt.L: Pois, ainda que [sejam] como espinhos entrelaçados \q e embriagados como com a sua bebida, \q serão consumidos \q como restolho completamente seco.
pt.B: Embora sejam como um emaranhado de espinhos \q e estejam bêbados com o seu vinho, \q serão queimados \q como restolho seco.
pt.R: Eles são como um monte de espinheiros emaranhados, \q como bêbados encharcados de vinho. \q Mas vão ser queimados \q como palha seca.

decisions.choice: a very difficult verse: entangled thorns, drunkards, dry stubble
alternatives: until they are like entangled thorns
decisions.reason: Almost every phrase of this verse is hard. The first words may mean "though they are like thorns" or "until they are like thorns"; "drunk with their drink" is a play on similar-sounding words; and the last word, "fully", may belong with the next verse. The general sense is clear: however strong and tangled the enemy is, and however much they drink, they will be burned up as quickly as dry straw.

decisions.choice: thorns and stubble burn quickly
decisions.reason: Thorn bushes and stubble catch fire at once and burn out fast (Isaiah 10:17; Psalm 118:12; Malachi 3:19). Drunkenness returns in 3:11, where Nineveh is told she will be made drunk with the cup of judgment.

decisions.choice: drunkards soaked in wine; dry straw
decisions.reason: Readable says "soaked in wine" for "drunk with their drink" and "straw" for "stubble".

decisions.choice: "마른 그루터기처럼" placed before the verb, in the third line
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb last, so the comparison of the Hebrew's last line comes before "삼켜질 것이다"; the four lines are kept, each with its own part of the verse.

en.R: Nineveh, from you came a man \q who made evil plans against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q His advice was wicked and worthless.

vi.L: Từ ngươi đã ra \q kẻ mưu tính điều ác nghịch cùng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q một mưu sĩ của sự vô dụng.
vi.B: Từ ngươi đã ra một kẻ \q mưu tính điều ác nghịch cùng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q một mưu sĩ gian ác.
vi.R: Hỡi Ni-ni-ve, từ ngươi đã xuất hiện một người \q lập mưu ác chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Lời khuyên của hắn thật gian ác và vô dụng.

ko.L: 너에게서 \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 거슬러 악을 꾀하는 자, \q 쓸모없는 모사가 나왔다.
ko.B: 너에게서 한 사람이 나왔다. \q 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 거슬러 악을 꾀하는 자, \q 악한 계략을 세우는 자다.
ko.R: 니느웨야, 너에게서 한 사람이 나왔다. \q 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 거슬러 악한 계획을 세웠다. \q 그의 계략은 악하고 쓸모없었다.

pt.L: De ti saiu \q um que trama o mal contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q um conselheiro de vileza.
pt.B: De ti saiu alguém \q que trama o mal contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q um conselheiro perverso.
pt.R: Nínive, de ti saiu um homem \q que fez planos maus contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. \q Os conselhos dele eram perversos e sem valor.

decisions.choice: from you: from Nineveh
decisions.reason: "You" is feminine singular. After the plural of verse 9 the poem turns to a city, which is Nineveh (1:1; 2:2).

decisions.choice: one who plots evil against the LORD: an Assyrian king
decisions.reason: The text does not name him. The words fit an Assyrian king who planned against Jerusalem, such as Sennacherib, who besieged it in 701 BC and mocked the LORD (2 Kings 18:13-35; Isaiah 36-37). The same pattern of plotting and defeat is then applied to Nineveh's rulers as a whole.

decisions.choice: worthlessness: the wickedness of one who is good for nothing
decisions.reason: The word joins "without" and "use" or "profit". It describes people who are worthless and wicked (Deuteronomy 13:14; 1 Samuel 2:12). In later Jewish writing it became a name for the devil, Belial (2 Corinthians 6:15); here it describes the Assyrian. It returns in 2:1.

decisions.choice: a counselor of wickedness (B); his advice was wicked and worthless (R); Nineveh (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "wickedness" for the Hebrew word, which carries both senses (m3); Readable keeps both. Readable names Nineveh, the "you" of the verse (m1).

decisions.choice: Nineveh addressed as "tú", with feminine agreement where Spanish shows it (3:5-19)
alternatives: vosotros / ustedes for the city's people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is feminine singular, the city (m1). As the term sheet says for Nineveh in Nahum 2-3, Spanish speaks to her as one woman ("tú"); the Assyrian king of 1:14 and 3:18 is masculine "tú", and Judah of 1:12-13 and 2:1 is "tú" too.

decisions.choice: Nineveh addressed as "tu", with feminine agreement throughout the book
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is feminine singular, the city (m1). As the term sheet says for personified cities, Nineveh takes "tu" and feminine agreement ("tu seras ivre", "cachée"); Judah of 1:12-13 is feminine too ("je t'ai affligée"), and the king of Assyria (1:14; 3:18) is masculine.

decisions.choice: Nineveh is addressed as "ngươi" at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note: foreign cities and nations are "ngươi" at every level.

decisions.choice: tu (ti, teu) for Nineveh, for Judah (1:12-13; 2:1) and for the Assyrian king (1:14); vocês for a group (1:9)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the city addressed as one woman (m1) is "tu", as God and the prophets speak to a city or a people as one in the Old Testament; the same "tu" goes to Judah and to the king of Assyria, and feminine forms where Portuguese shows gender ("tu também ficarás embriagada", 3:11). A group addressed in the plural is "vocês".

decisions.choice: um conselheiro de vileza (L); um conselheiro perverso (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word joins worthlessness and wickedness (m3). "Vileza" carries both at Literal, as "vil" means base and of no worth; Balanced says "perverso", as the English Balanced says "wickedness"; Readable keeps both with "perversos e sem valor".

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִם־שְׁלֵמִים֙ וְכֵ֣ן רַבִּ֔ים וְכֵ֥ן נָגֹ֖זּוּ וְעָבָ֑ר וְעִ֨נִּתִ֔ךְ לֹ֥א אֲעַנֵּ֖ךְ עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: Though [they are] whole and likewise many, even so they will be cut off, and he will pass away; and I have afflicted you, I will not afflict you again.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Though [they are] at full strength and likewise many, \q even so they will be sheared off, and he will pass away. \q I have afflicted you; \q I will not afflict you again.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Though they are at full strength and many, \q they will still be cut down and pass away. \q I have afflicted you, \q but I will afflict you no more.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Even though the Assyrians are strong and have many soldiers, \q they will be cut down and disappear. \q People of Judah, I have made you suffer, \q but I will not make you suffer again.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Aunque [estén] enteros y asimismo sean muchos, \q aun así serán cortados, y él pasará. \q Te he afligido; \q no te afligiré más.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Aunque estén en plena fuerza y sean muchos, \q aun así serán cortados y desaparecerán. \q Te he afligido, \q pero no te afligiré más.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Aunque los asirios son fuertes y tienen muchos soldados, \q serán derribados y desaparecerán. \q Pueblo de Judá, te he hecho sufrir, \q pero no te haré sufrir más.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Même [s’ils sont] intacts et aussi nombreux, \q même ainsi ils seront tondus, et il passera. \q Je t’ai affligé ; \q je ne t’affligerai plus.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Même s’ils sont en pleine force et nombreux, \q ils seront pourtant fauchés et disparaîtront. \q Je t’ai affligé, \q mais je ne t’affligerai plus.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Même si les Assyriens sont forts et ont beaucoup de soldats, \q ils seront abattus et ils disparaîtront. \q Peuple de Juda, je t’ai fait souffrir, \q mais je ne te ferai plus souffrir.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Ingawa [wako] kamili na pia wengi, \q hata hivyo watakatiliwa mbali, naye atapita. \q Nimekutesa; \q sitakutesa tena.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Ingawa wana nguvu kamili na ni wengi, \q hata hivyo watakatwa na kutoweka. \q Nimekutesa, \q lakini sitakutesa tena.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Ingawa Waashuru wana nguvu na askari wengi, \q watakatwa na kutoweka. \q Enyi watu wa Yuda, nimewafanya mteseke, \q lakini sitawatesa tena.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Dù [chúng] còn nguyên sức mạnh và đông đúc như vậy, \q dầu vậy chúng sẽ bị cắt đi, và nó sẽ qua đi. \q Ta đã làm khổ ngươi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không làm khổ ngươi nữa.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Dù chúng còn nguyên sức mạnh và đông đảo, \q chúng vẫn sẽ bị đốn hạ và biến mất. \q Ta đã làm cho con khốn khổ, \q nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không làm cho con khốn khổ nữa.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Dù quân A-si-ri mạnh mẽ và có nhiều binh lính, \q chúng sẽ bị đốn hạ và biến mất. \q Hỡi dân Giu-đa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho các con đau khổ, \q nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không làm cho các con đau khổ nữa.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 그들이 힘이 온전하고 수가 많을지라도, \q 그렇게 그들이 베어지고 그가 사라질 것이다. \q 내가 너를 괴롭게 하였으나, \q 다시는 너를 괴롭게 하지 않겠다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 그들이 힘이 넘치고 수가 많을지라도, \q 그들은 베어져 사라질 것이다. \q 내가 너를 괴롭게 하였으나, \q 이제는 더 이상 너를 괴롭게 하지 않겠다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 앗시리아 사람들이 강하고 군사가 많을지라도, \q 그들은 베어져 사라질 것이다. \q 유다 백성아, 내가 너희를 고통스럽게 하였지만, \q 다시는 너희를 고통스럽게 하지 않겠다.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Ainda que [estejam] com toda a força e igualmente numerosos, \q mesmo assim serão tosquiados, e ele passará. \q Eu te afligi; \q não te afligirei mais.
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Ainda que estejam com toda a força e sejam muitos, \q mesmo assim serão cortados e desaparecerão. \q Eu te afligi, \q mas não te afligirei mais.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Mesmo que os assírios sejam fortes e tenham muitos soldados, \q eles serão derrubados e vão desaparecer. \q Povo de Judá, eu te fiz sofrer, \q mas não vou fazer-te sofrer de novo.

decisions.choice: they ... you: the LORD speaks of the Assyrians and to Judah
decisions.reason: "They" are the Assyrians. "You" is feminine singular and is Judah, pictured as a woman, as 2:1 makes plain. The poem keeps turning from one to the other: verse 11 speaks to Nineveh, verses 12-13 to Judah, verse 14 to the Assyrian king, and 2:1 to Judah again. The verb "pass away" is singular, perhaps thinking of the army as one body or of its king.

decisions.choice: at full strength: whole, unharmed and complete in number
decisions.reason: The word means whole or complete. It may describe the Assyrians as at full strength, or as having allies; the parallel "many" favors their numbers and strength. The point is that being strong will not save them.

decisions.choice: I have afflicted you: Assyria was the LORD's rod for Judah
decisions.reason: The prophets say that the LORD used Assyria to discipline his people (Isaiah 10:5-6). That discipline is now over. Nahum does not say that Judah was never at fault, but that the LORD's punishment through Assyria has come to an end.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); The LORD says this (B); This is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the formula in the prophets (Isaiah). God's words follow without quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the Assyrians ... have many soldiers; People of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable names the two groups the verse speaks of and to (m1), since the Hebrew does it only by "they" and "you".

decisions.choice: "Así dice el SEÑOR:" (L); "El SEÑOR dice esto:" (B); "Esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR:" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled prophetic formula, recorded here at its first use in Nahum.

decisions.choice: the LORD speaks to Judah as "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B) / "các con" (R, "dân Giu-đa")
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: the LORD speaks of the Assyrians and to Judah; this is a promise, so the Isaiah note's "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B, R) applies, and Readable is plural because it names the people.

decisions.choice: "Thus says the LORD" as its own sentence ending in a period
decisions.reason: As the term sheets: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다" (L), "이렇게 말씀하신다" (B), "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다" (R); God's words that follow are 해라체 without quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "BWANA asema hivi:" (L); "Hivi ndivyo BWANA asemavyo:" (B); "Hili ndilo BWANA analosema:" (R)
decisions.reason: "Thus says the LORD" as in 2 Kings 19:6 and the term sheet; recorded once for Nahum.

decisions.choice: Assim diz o SENHOR (L, B); É isto que o SENHOR diz (R)
decisions.reason: The formula takes the wording Isaiah and Jeremiah settled in Portuguese for the prophets, with God's words following without quotation marks, as in the English.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה אֶשְׁבֹּ֥ר מֹטֵ֖הוּ מֵֽעָלָ֑יִךְ וּמוֹסְרֹתַ֖יִךְ אֲנַתֵּֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And now I will break his yoke-bar from on you, and your bonds I will tear apart.

en.L: And now I will break his yoke from upon you, \q and I will tear apart your bonds.
en.B: Now I will break his yoke from off you \q and snap the ropes that bind you.
en.R: Now I will break the yoke the Assyrians put on you. \q I will tear off the ropes that tie you up.

es.L: Y ahora quebraré su yugo de sobre ti, \q y romperé tus ataduras.
es.B: Ahora quebraré el yugo que él te puso \q y romperé las cuerdas que te atan.
es.R: Ahora romperé el yugo que los asirios te pusieron. \q Arrancaré las cuerdas que te tienen atado.

fr.L: Et maintenant je briserai son joug de dessus toi, \q et je romprai tes liens.
fr.B: Maintenant, je briserai son joug qui pèse sur toi \q et je romprai les cordes qui t’attachent.
fr.R: Maintenant, je briserai le joug que les Assyriens t’ont mis sur le cou. \q J’arracherai les cordes qui te lient.

sw.L: Na sasa nitaivunja nira yake juu yako, \q na kuvikata vifungo vyako.
sw.B: Sasa nitaivunja nira yake iliyo juu yako \q na kuzikata kamba zinazokufunga.
sw.R: Sasa nitaivunja nira ambayo Waashuru wamekuwekea. \q Nitazikata kamba zilizokufunga.

vi.L: Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ bẻ gãy ách của nó khỏi ngươi, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ bứt đứt các dây trói ngươi.
vi.B: Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ bẻ gãy ách nó đè trên con \q và giật đứt các dây trói buộc con.
vi.R: Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ bẻ gãy cái ách quân A-si-ri đặt trên các con. \q Ta sẽ giật đứt các dây trói các con.

ko.L: 이제 내가 그의 멍에를 네 위에서 꺾고, \q 너의 결박을 끊어 버리겠다.
ko.B: 이제 내가 그가 네게 씌운 멍에를 꺾고, \q 너를 묶은 줄을 끊어 버리겠다.
ko.R: 이제 나는 앗시리아 사람들이 너희에게 씌운 멍에를 꺾겠다. \q 너희를 묶은 줄을 끊어 버리겠다.

pt.L: E agora quebrarei o jugo dele de cima de ti \q e romperei as tuas amarras.
pt.B: Agora quebrarei o jugo dele, que está sobre ti, \q e arrebentarei as cordas que te prendem.
pt.R: Agora vou quebrar o jugo que os assírios puseram sobre ti. \q Vou arrancar as cordas que te amarram.

decisions.choice: his yoke ... your bonds: Assyria's rule over Judah
decisions.reason: A yoke is the wooden bar laid on the neck of an ox, held by ropes or straps. It is a common picture of foreign rule and the tribute it demanded (Isaiah 10:27; Jeremiah 27:2; 28:10-14). "His" is the Assyrian, the oppressor of verses 11 and 14.

decisions.choice: Judah under Assyria
decisions.reason: From the time of King Ahaz (about 734 BC) Judah was a subject state of Assyria and paid it heavy tribute (2 Kings 16:7-8; 18:14). Hezekiah's revolt led to Sennacherib's invasion in 701 BC, and Manasseh remained a subject of Assyria.

decisions.choice: the ropes that bind you (B); the Assyrians (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ropes" for the bonds that hold a yoke in place. Readable names the Assyrians as the "he" whose yoke it is (m1).

source.text: וְצִוָּ֤ה עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה לֹֽא־יִזָּרַ֥ע מִשִּׁמְךָ֖ ע֑וֹד מִבֵּ֨ית אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אַכְרִ֨ית פֶּ֧סֶל וּמַסֵּכָ֛ה אָשִׂ֥ים קִבְרֶ֖ךָ כִּ֥י קַלּֽוֹתָ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh has commanded concerning you: Not will be sown from your name again; from [the] house of your gods I will cut off carved image and cast image; I will make your grave, for you are of no account.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded concerning you: \q No more [offspring] of your name will be sown; \q from the house of your gods I will cut off carved image and cast image; I will make your grave, for you are of no account.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given a command about you: \q you will have no more offspring to bear your name. \q I will cut off the carved idol and the cast image from the house of your gods. I will make your grave, for you count for nothing.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given an order about you, king of Assyria: \q You will have no children to carry on your name. \q I will destroy the idols and metal statues in the temple of your gods. I will dig your grave, because you are worthless.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dado orden acerca de ti: \q no se sembrará más [descendencia] de tu nombre; \q de la casa de tus dioses extirparé la imagen tallada y la imagen fundida; haré tu sepulcro, porque eres despreciable.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dado una orden acerca de ti: \q no tendrás más descendientes que lleven tu nombre. \q Eliminaré de la casa de tus dioses el ídolo tallado y la imagen de metal fundido. Prepararé tu sepulcro, porque no vales nada.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dado una orden acerca de ti, rey de Asiria: \q No tendrás hijos que lleven tu nombre. \q Destruiré los ídolos y las estatuas de metal que hay en el templo de tus dioses. Cavaré tu tumba, porque no vales nada.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a ordonné à ton sujet : \q On ne sèmera plus de ton nom ; \q de la maison de tes dieux je retrancherai l’image taillée et l’image de fonte ; je ferai ta tombe, car tu es méprisable.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné un ordre à ton sujet : \q tu n’auras plus de descendants pour porter ton nom. \q Je retrancherai de la maison de tes dieux l’idole sculptée et l’image de métal fondu. Je préparerai ta tombe, car tu ne comptes pour rien.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné un ordre à ton sujet, roi d’Assyrie : \q Tu n’auras pas d’enfants pour porter ton nom. \q Je détruirai les idoles et les statues de métal dans le temple de tes dieux. Je creuserai ta tombe, parce que tu ne vaux rien.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameamuru kuhusu wewe: \q Hakuna tena [uzao] utakaopandwa kwa jina lako; \q kutoka nyumba ya miungu yako nitakatilia mbali sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya kusubu; nitalifanya kaburi lako, kwa maana wewe si kitu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametoa amri kuhusu wewe: \q hutakuwa tena na uzao wa kulibeba jina lako. \q Nitaikatilia mbali sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya kusubu kutoka nyumba ya miungu yako. Nitalifanya kaburi lako, kwa maana wewe huna thamani.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametoa amri kuhusu wewe, mfalme wa Ashuru: \q Hutakuwa na watoto wa kuendeleza jina lako. \q Nitaziangamiza sanamu na vinyago vya chuma katika hekalu la miungu yako. Nitakuchimbia kaburi lako, kwa sababu wewe hufai kitu.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền lệnh về ngươi: \q Dòng dõi mang danh ngươi sẽ không còn được gieo nữa; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ diệt trừ tượng chạm và tượng đúc khỏi đền các thần của ngươi; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm mồ mả cho ngươi, vì ngươi chẳng ra gì.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ra lệnh về ngươi: \q ngươi sẽ không còn dòng dõi để mang danh ngươi. \q Ta sẽ diệt trừ tượng chạm và tượng đúc khỏi đền các thần của ngươi. Ta sẽ đào mồ cho ngươi, vì ngươi chẳng đáng gì.
vi.R: Hỡi vua A-si-ri, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ra lệnh về ngươi: \q Ngươi sẽ không có con cháu để nối dõi tông đường. \q Ta sẽ hủy phá các thần tượng và tượng đúc trong đền thờ các thần của ngươi. Ta sẽ đào mồ chôn ngươi, vì ngươi thật vô dụng.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에 관하여 명령하셨다. \q 네 이름에서 [자손이] 다시는 뿌려지지 않을 것이다. \q 내가 네 신들의 신전에서 새긴 우상과 부어 만든 우상을 끊어 버리겠다. 내가 네 무덤을 만들겠으니, 네가 하찮기 때문이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에 관하여 명령하셨다. \q 네 이름을 이을 자손이 다시는 없을 것이다. \q 내가 네 신들의 신전에서 새긴 우상과 부어 만든 우상을 없애 버리겠다. 내가 네 무덤을 파겠다. 너는 아무것도 아니기 때문이다.
ko.R: 앗시리아 왕아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에 관하여 명령하셨다. \q 너에게는 네 이름을 이어 갈 자식이 없을 것이다. \q 내가 네 신들의 신전에 있는 우상들과 쇠붙이로 만든 신상들을 없애 버리겠다. 내가 네 무덤을 파겠다. 너는 쓸모없는 자이기 때문이다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu ordem a teu respeito: \q não será mais semeado [descendente] do teu nome; \q da casa dos teus deuses cortarei a imagem esculpida e a imagem fundida; farei a tua sepultura, pois és insignificante.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} deu uma ordem a teu respeito: \q não terás mais descendentes que levem o teu nome. \q Da casa dos teus deuses eliminarei o ídolo esculpido e a imagem fundida. Prepararei a tua sepultura, pois não vales nada.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} deu uma ordem a teu respeito, rei da Assíria: \q não vais ter filhos para continuar o teu nome. \q Vou destruir os ídolos e as estátuas de metal no templo dos teus deuses. Vou cavar a tua sepultura, porque não tens valor.

decisions.choice: you: the king of Assyria
alternatives: the people of Nineveh as a whole
decisions.reason: "You" is now masculine singular. It is most likely the king of Assyria, who is addressed by name in 3:18, though it could be Nineveh's people taken as one.

decisions.choice: no more will be sown from your name: you will have no descendants
decisions.reason: Seed is the Hebrew word for offspring. To have no more "sown" of one's name is to have no descendants to keep it alive (compare Isaiah 14:22). The king's line, and with it the empire, will end.

decisions.choice: carved image and cast image in the house of your gods
decisions.reason: A carved image was cut from wood or stone; a cast image was made of molten metal (Deuteronomy 27:15). The house of the gods is a temple. Sennacherib was killed by his own sons while he worshiped in the temple of his god (2 Kings 19:37), and the gods of Nineveh could not save it.

decisions.choice: I will make your grave, for you are of no account
alternatives: I will make the house of your gods your grave
decisions.reason: "Of no account" is literally "light", without weight or honor, the opposite of "heavy", which is the word for glory. The first clause may also be read "I will make it (the house of your gods) your grave".

decisions.choice: no more offspring to bear your name (B); no children to carry on your name (R); worthless (B, R); king of Assyria (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the picture of sowing (m2). Readable names the king of Assyria as the one addressed (m1), and marks it as likely rather than certain.

decisions.choice: The LORD's command to the king of Assyria in 해라체 with "너"
decisions.reason: The verse is addressed to the king of Assyria (meaning decision); the narrator's line gives God -시-, and God's own words that follow are 해라체 without -시-.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria is "ngươi" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: "you" is the king of Assyria; the terms note gives foreign kings "ngươi" at every level. Literal keeps the Hebrew picture "sown", Balanced and Readable say descendants.

decisions.choice: "extirparé" (L); "Eliminaré" (B)
decisions.reason: The same verbs as Micah 5:9-12 for "cut off".

decisions.choice: pois és insignificante
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "light", without weight or honour (m4); "leve" would be read as a compliment or as weight alone, so Literal says "insignificante", one of no account, as the English Literal does. Balanced says "não vales nada" and Readable "não tens valor".
